title: Scalar enhancement of an additive stalk equivalence
statement: Let C have objects in Type(u+1) and morphisms in Type u, J a topology, p a Type-u point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], G a topological group and R a commutative ring in Type v. Put w=max(u+1,v). Given an equivalence from abelian sheaves of universe w to discrete integer G-representations of universe w and an additive natural isomorphism between its underlying abelian group functor and p.sheafFiber, there is an equivalence from R-module sheaves of universe w to discrete R-linear G-representations, with a module-linear natural stalk comparison. For any pair of lifts and section, an equality asserting that g sends the additive germ at the first lift to that at the second implies the corresponding equality of module germs.

proof.text: An equivalence between these preadditive categories is additive since it preserves binary products; the sheaf category has finite biproducts. Compose the module-sheaf scalar equivalence, the induced scalar equivalence, and the inverse representation scalar equivalence.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Compose the given additive stalk comparison with Point.sheafFiberCompIso for forgetting scalars. The result is linear: apply naturality to the scalar sheaf endomorphism. On the module stalk that endomorphism acts by multiplication, as follows by representing an element by a germ and using naturality and linearity of the germ map. The comparison is bijective and hence determines a module-linear natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: The stalk comparison for forgetting scalars preserves every germ. Apply injectivity of the module comparison to identify its inverse on a germ with the inverse additive comparison on the underlying germ. Substitute this equality and the assumed additive action formula; the germ comparison gives the module action formula.
